title: MemHarness — where the paper and the code part ways
subtitle: Only the divergent steps are drawn. Each node states both sides; the lane says which stage of the pipeline the divergence sits in.
source: paper arXiv:2607.28272  ×  repo KnowledgeXLab/MemHarness @ 31329e8   ·   servers/memharness/verification.md §5, 17 divergences found, 10 drawn here
footer: memory-bench · methodology flow · paper ↔ code divergence
legend_notes: Headline (D1): §3.4 says the trajectory-level advantage is shared equally across thinking, reconstruction and action tokens. Under the exact config both training scripts use (use_actor_rollout_wg=true), train_memory_adaptor_enabled() returns False -> the reconstruction completion enters zero gradient updates, from either path.

A6 doubles down: not only is reconstruction's credit cut off from the main GRPO update, a fully separate, independently-trainable adaptor-GRPO loop exists in the code (D9) — and neither training script enables it either. In the runs that produced the paper's numbers, reconstruction's own parameters most likely receive no task-reward gradient from anywhere.

B6 quietly does two things the paper doesn't describe: it reconstructs with a placeholder even when nothing was retrieved (D7), and it only ever shows the reconstruction model 1 of the k=3 hits it fetched — matching the paper's own Appendix C template over its own main-text Eq.3 (D6).

Not drawn (real findings, no stage-lane fit): D2 tag word order (<retrieve_memory> vs code's <memory_retrieve>); D3/D4 format-reward component weighting and think-block cardinality (reward-shaping internals, not a memory-pipeline step); D14 num_memories_per_trajectory=1 (paper gives no number); D16/D17 embedding-backend requirement and dedupe comparator (>= vs >).
